articles.headline: Yan Diomande, Kylian Mbappé lead Real Madrid rout of Sevilla
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé's brilliant double on Sunday helped Real Madrid prepare for next week's El Clasico with a 4-1 triumph over Sevilla at the Bernabeu.
articles.headlineJa: ヤン・ディオマンデとキリアン・エムバペが主導し、レアル・マドリードがセビージャを圧倒
articles.descriptionJa: 日曜日にキリアン・エムバペが鮮やかな2ゴールを決め、レアル・マドリードはベルナベウでセビージャに4-1で勝利し、来週のエル・クラシコに向けて弾みをつけた。
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé's brilliant double on Sunday helped Real Madrid prepare for next week's El Clasico with a 4-1 triumph over Sevilla at the Bernabeu.

The France striker finished off a fine team move in style to double Madrid's lead in the 37th minute after Arda Güler put the hosts ahead with a curling strike on the half hour.

Mbappé extended their advantage with a Panenka penalty after the break and although Manu Bueno scored a consolation goal, Yan Diomande soon fired home to wrap up the three points.

Victory comes just days after earning a stunning 4-3 comeback win over Jose Mourinho's former club Roma in the Champions League and ahead of a huge week for Los Blancos.

They return to European action against RB Leipzig on Wednesday before Sunday's trip to the Spotify Camp Nou, where Madrid take on LaLiga leaders Barcelona, who have started the domestic season with nine straight wins.

Madrid pulled off the one-sided win without the services of Vinícius Júnior, who is serving the first of a four-game ban for pulling the hair of Villarreal's Nathan Saliba last weekend.

Information from PA was used in this recap.

articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationの記者たちが、日曜日の各試合から生じた最大の疑問に答えながら、全ての展開に反応します。第6週から得られた知見がこちらです。
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in London with a thrilling matchup between the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars. 

Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. made his much-anticipated Texans debut, but it was quarterback C.J. Stroud who was the star of this day as Houston was able to hold off the Jaguars in a thriller.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

HOU-JAX

Catch up on Thursday's game:

SEA-DEN

Houston 34, Jacksonville 31

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Texans

Can quarterback C.J. Stroud keep this hot start going? Even though Stroud did have an ill-timed interception that gave the Jaguars a chance late in the fourth quarter, he was stellar. The fourth-year quarterback is continuing to perform at an MVP level, but against the Jaguars, Houston needed him at his best -- and he delivered. He led the game-winning drive to cap a 306-yard, three-touchdown outing in his first London performance.

Trend to watch: The Texans' "elite" defense has been far from it. Coach DeMeco Ryans took over playcalling this week, but his unit allowed 31 points. It's the third time this season that the Texans have allowed at least 30 points. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: vs. Giants (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Jaguars

Is it time for the Jaguars to fully unleash Travis Hunter on offense? They may need to. Hunter had his best offensive game of the season. He caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown after having just two catches for 17 yards in the first five games. The Jaguars needed him to step up because receiver Brian Thomas Jr. struggled, dropping two passes -- including one that would have given the Jaguars a chance to attempt a long field goal at the end of the first half. Thomas, who had an issue with drops last year, didn't play an offensive snap in the second half after playing 15 in the first. Hunter, with a bigger offensive workload, could make up for Thomas' struggles.

Trend to watch: The Jaguars are banged up at safety, with Antonio Johnson leaving the game with an ankle injury. They were already down Caleb Ransaw (IR) and went to Kaevon Merriweather, who was on the practice squad until he was signed to the active roster before last week's game. With the bye next week, the Jaguars need to get healthy and possibly make another move depending on how long Johnson is out. -- Michael DiRocco

Next game: vs. Colts (Nov. 1, 1 p.m. ET)

articles.headline: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter's 2026 season: A career best in Week 6?
articles.description: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
articles.headlineJa: ジャガーズのCB/WRトラビス・ハンターの2026年シーズンを追う：第6週にキャリアハイを更新するか？
articles.descriptionJa: 毎週、この二刀流のコーナーバック兼レシーバーが、攻撃と守備でそれぞれ何スナップ出場したかを検証します。起用法に傾向はあるのでしょうか。
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. However, unlike his rookie season, the plan was for the 2025 No. 2 overall pick to be a starter on defense. Now, he is just being mixed in on offense with a specific package of plays. The situation is fluid, though, and head coach Liam Coen has maintained that Hunter's usage could change weekly.

"You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches [on offense], then [he] absolutely will."

Hunter played more on offense than defense in his 2025 rookie season, which ended after seven games because of a right knee injury. The 2024 Heisman Trophy winner had 28 catches for 298 yards and a touchdown and 15 tackles and three pass breakups. He played 67% of the team's offensive snaps and 36% of the defensive snaps before his injury, which occurred during practice on Oct. 30.

How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

Week 6 vs. Houston Texans in London

Hunter had the best game of his career against the Texans at Wembley Stadium, catching four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown and also intercepting C.J. Stroud in the end zone. He's just the fourth player since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger with a receiving touchdown and interception in the same game and the first to do it since Philadelphia's Brian Dawkins in 2002. The touchdown and interception came on consecutive drives.

Per NFL Next Gen Stats, Hunter had 34 coverage snaps and limited the Texans to two catches on five targets. However, he also was hit with a questionable pass interference penalty in the end zone against Nico Collins that gave the Texans the ball at the 1-yard line late in the first half. Despite that, this was the first time Hunter has made a significant impact on both sides of the ball -- 58 snaps on defense and 9 on offense (season high) -- in the same game in his 13 career games. 

Week 5 vs. Philadelphia Eagles in London

Hunter played every defensive snap (59) for the second week in a row and had six tackles (second-most on the team) and a pass breakup. He was penalized for defensive pass interference that wiped out a third-and-17 incompletion in the second quarter. It gave the Eagles the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line and Philadelphia running back Will Shipley scored two plays later.

On offense, Hunter played five snaps and touched the ball for the first time since Week 1, catching a 9-yard pass on second-and-7 from the Jaguars' 40-yard line. Parker Washington scored on a 51-yard catch-and-run on the next play.

Everything that happens in sports has additional context when viewed from a sports betting perspective. From season-changing injuries to record-setting moments and so much more, the sports news cycle will constantly and significantly affect the sports betting industry.

Our NFL betting buzz file, with contributions from David Purdum, Doug Greenberg and others, aims to provide fans a look at the sports betting stories that are driving the conversation throughout each week of the season. 

Key links: NFL futures | Awards odds | Sports betting home | DraftKings 

Oct. 18: NFL survivor player says proxy error cost him $100K entry and shot at $7.7M

By David Purdum

A first-time contestant in a high-stakes NFL survivor pool says the proxy service he hired to submit his picks failed to get this week's selection in by the deadline, costing him his $100,000 buy-in and a shot at the $7.7 million prize pool.

Sam Lee, a 42-year-old lawyer in Houston, told ESPN that his proxy for the Circa Grandissimo contest called him roughly 20 minutes after Saturday's 4 p.m. PT deadline to let him know they did not get the selection submitted in time. Picks must be submitted by someone in Nevada, so out-of-state players often hire proxy services.

This is the second year that the Las Vegas casino has hosted the Grandissimo contest. It's believed to be the first time a pick in the contest has not been entered by the deadline.

Lee said he entered his pick -- the Los Angeles Rams -- on the proxy service's online portal Friday. Lee said a proxy representative apologized and said they "forgot" to submit the pick.

"I was pissed," Lee said.

The Rams play the Arizona Cardinals in late afternoon games Sunday. With only 15 contestants remaining ahead of Week 6, Lee's entry -- named Parlay Sam -- had an estimated value of $513,333, according to Circa.

Lee said he decided to enter his first Grandissimo at the last minute and flew into Las Vegas on Sept. 9 with over $100,000 cash for his entry fee. He said he hired his proxy after signing up.

When reached by ESPN on Sunday, Lee declined to identify the proxy service and said he's exploring all his options. Circa did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

"This isn't over," Lee said.

Oct. 11: Who wants to win the NFC East?

By Doug Greenberg

Week 5 was one to forget for the NFC East, to say the least.

It started Thursday night when the Dallas Cowboys lost outright to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after closing as 8.5-point favorites, tied with four other games as the biggest upset of the season, according to DraftKings odds.

Not only were the Cowboys heavily backed on the spread and in moneyline parlays at multiple sportsbooks, they were also the most popular pick in both ESPN Survivor (40% of the remaining field) and the $1,000-per-entry Circa Survivor (2,554 entries, 42.8% of the remaining field). articles.headline: Dominic Calvert-Lewin 'showed respect by standing' as others took knee for racism campaign - Daniel Farke
articles.description: Leeds boss Daniel Farke has said that striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin showed "respect" after not taking the knee prior to Leeds United's draw with Manchester United on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: 「他の選手が人種差別反対キャンペーンで膝をつく中、ドミニク・カルバート＝レウィンは立ち上がることで敬意を示した」— ダニエル・ファーケ
articles.descriptionJa: リーズのダニエル・ファーケ監督は、日曜日のマンチェスター・ユナイテッドとの引き分け前の試合において、ストライカーのドミニク・カルバート＝レウィンが膝をつかなかったことは「敬意」の表れであったと語った。
articles.body:
Leeds boss Daniel Farke has said that striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin showed "respect" after not taking the knee prior to Leeds United's draw with Manchester United on Sunday.

Players have taken the knee across Premier League fixtures this weekend as a part of the league's "No Room for Racism" campaign, but Calvert-Lewin joined the few who opted against, with Ainsley Maitland-Niles, Issa Diop and Marc Guéhi also choosing to stand before their games on Saturday.

Speaking after the game at Elland Road, Farke defended Calvert-Lewin's decision and praised the Premier League's initiative. 

"Dom [Calvert-Lewin] is more or less like, 'No, I don't go down. I show my respect by standing up,' every individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way," Farke said.

"It's definitely a good campaign and a good topic that football and sports, in general, support situations like this because a dressing room is a perfect example of how we should all live together.

"Different passports, different languages, different religions, but they are all together as human beings and friends who work together toward one target. This is how the world should be."

The league's campaign aligns with Black History Month and the gesture was introduced in 2020 after the murder of George Floyd by former police officer Derek Chauvin in the United States.

Then of Crystal Palace, Wilfred Zaha was the first player to opt against taking the knee before a game in 2021.

articles.headline: Arsenal don't look ready to 'attack' the Premier League title like they want to -- yet
articles.description: Defending Premier League champions Arsenal put in a weak attacking performance at Nottingham Forest -- but maybe that's just fine.
articles.headlineJa: アーセナルは、彼らが望むほどプレミアリーグ優勝へ「攻め」の姿勢を見せられていない――まだ、だが
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグ王者アーセナルは、ノッティンガム・フォレスト戦で精彩を欠く攻撃を見せた。しかし、それはそれで良いのかもしれない。
articles.body:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta claimed on the eve of this season that he wanted his side to "attack the title" rather than defend it. We're all still waiting to see the Gunners shift into gear.

Of course, it might not matter. The Gunners' impressive squad depth was on show once more Sunday as Noni Madueke's deflected 80th-minute winner secured a hard-fought 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.

It is their 10th win from 11 matches across all competitions this season and -- assuming Manchester City are punished for their 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules -- then Arsenal are the overwhelming favorites to retain the league they won for the first time in 22 years.

Their only defeat thus far came at Brighton prior to the international break, and results offer Arteta an easy counter to any suggestion they had to regain their momentum in three matches since.

"You play 11 games, you win 10 and you lose momentum? So, what is it then? Then you have to win every game and that's extremely difficult to do and nobody else does it," he said, understandably.

But Sunday offered another game where you would've been entitled to expect a little more -- especially given Arteta's desire to dominate opponents with greater conviction than they managed last season.

It was an example of the sort of word-play Arteta likes. By definition, champions are tasked with "defending" the title but Arteta challenged the inherent caution in that phrase, instead urging his players to go on the front foot in search of more silverware.

They ended Sunday with 75% possession -- more than they had in any league game last season -- but just one shot on target. It was, in truth, a tough watch.

Some of that was down to Forest's 5-4-1 shape and diligent rearguard action, which was restricted to sporadic counterattacks as Liam Delap tried his best to carry the fight, often alone, in the final third.

But there is a sense that this Arsenal side is still yet to become the all-conquering force Arteta wants it to be. For long periods at Forest, it was easy for minds to drift back to the summer, when the club went in search of a top-class addition to its forward line only to end up empty-handed.

Christos Tzolis arrived from Club Brugge and started the season well prior to his current hamstring injury but Arsenal laid the groundwork in deals for Morgan Rogers, Vinícius Júnior and Julián Álvarez in vain.

Arteta is consequently left to shuffle what he must feel is an incomplete pack. Left wing, the issue identified all summer, remains unconvincing and it is an enduring irony of Sunday's victory that the goal came from that flank.

With Tzolis absent, expectations were high that Eberechi Eze could seize a chance to kick-start his Arsenal career. Twenty-one touches and one moment where he ran the ball out of play aimlessly later, he was hauled off at halftime for Madueke.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta puts stale Arsenal display down to Nottingham Forest tactics: 'They put a Christmas tree there'
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has defended his Arsenal team after they only managed one shot on target in their 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: ミケル・アルテタ、アーセナルの精彩を欠いたプレーはノッティンガム・フォレストの戦術のせいだと語る：「彼らはクリスマスツリー（の布陣）を敷いていた」
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタは、日曜日のノッティンガム・フォレスト戦で1-0と勝利したものの、枠内シュートがわずか1本に留まったアーセナルのチームを擁護した。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has defended his Arsenal team after they only managed one shot on target in their 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

Noni Madueke's deflected strike in the 80th minute was the only time the Gunners mustered a shot on goal, and although it was enough for a valuable win, Arteta's side were toothless for the vast majority of the contest.

"I think we have played 11 competitive matches. We won 10. So we're going to gain the variety of ways to win in many different contexts," Arteta said.

"We knew we wouldn't score in the first 20, 30 minutes. We weren't going to face a different Forest because they are extremely well coached. They put a Christmas tree there. There is no space to play. You have to be so neat and tidy.

"You have to otherwise generate a lot of chaos in the box, whether it is in open play or with set-pieces.

"We did a couple of times and created two big chances. We didn't even hit the target, which is the difference.

"And the longer the game goes, we say, 'OK, now we have to play a different game because [at] the moment we start to ramp up our level of frustration.'

"But we got the goal."

Madueke -- who was left out of Thomas Tuchel's most recent England squad -- was introduced as a half-time substitute for the ineffective Eberechi Eze, and Arteta paid tribute to the 24-year-old's attitude.

"Noni, look at me, a smile on my face because he's a special character," Arteta said. "He's someone very much loved in and around the dressing room, the way he connects, talks to people.

"He's just a special guy. I think I saw an interview where they were asking a few of our players, 'Who would you call if you have a problem?'

"And some of them said Noni, which I was surprised [by].

"But I think it's a massive credit and explains the kind of person that he is. He's in a good moment.

"I think after the break, he's showing something else, another level of anger, another level of conviction as well in his actions, and he's becoming now decisive in matches, which is what we expect for a player like him."

It was a third 1-0 home defeat of the season for Forest, who are struggling to adapt to life under Oliver Glasner, and they have not scored in five home matches in all competitions after missing two big late chances.

This was also a third league defeat in a row and they now sit in the relegation zone after seven games.

"Five interviews, five times the same question. I think that's the answer," Glasner said. "It feels very harsh, it feels unfair, but we have to accept it that we are missing some bits.

"Today I think the performance in many parts was really good defensively, was on a top level. Giving them one shot on target, and this one is deflected, and then you lose, it feels even tougher.

"What we are missing is in every single game we have our moments, but then we don't take them.

Trending rumors

- Viktor Gyökeres is prepared to leave Arsenal in January for more consistent game time, claims TEAMtalk. The report states that frustration over a lack of minutes has forced the Sweden international to consider his future with the Gunners, just over a year on from his initial £55 million move from Sporting CP. The 28-year-old has been restricted to three Premier League appearances so far this season, all from the bench, despite scoring 21 goals for Arsenal across all competitions last campaign. Atletico Madrid have been labelled as an interested party, while teams in Italy, Germany, and Spain have also been outlined as possible destinations.

The 26-year-old is being tracked by the Merseyside outfit as an option to bolster the backline, with his ability to play as both a centre-back and a right back viewed as highly desirable. Kalulu has a deal until 2029 with Juventus, and has featured in every game this season, suggesting any transfer could be difficult to secure.

 

- Manchester United are ready to dip into the January transfer market to bolster the backline amid concerns over the quality in the defensive ranks. Sky Sports reports that the club is looking at center backs and left backs who could make an impact, after spending the two previous summers improving the forward line and the midfield. It's unclear exactly what funds could be available to the recruitment team, amid growing pressure to improve after a difficult start to the season.

- Arsenal and Chelsea are both tracking the progress of Oliver Mansson, 17, during a breakthrough campaign for IFK Goteborg. That's according to TEAMtalk, who claim the midfielder has caught the eye of the two Premier League clubs, along with a whole host of other English clubs. Mansson has featured 17 times across all competitions this season, 13 of which have been in the Allsvenskan. The youngster has a deal until 2028 with Goteborg, which could prompt a move in the future, though he cannot officially move to the Premier League until next August, when he would turn 18.

articles.headline: Ruben Amorim still unbeaten in Serie A after Milan win
articles.description: AC Milan held off a fightback from Atalanta to close out a 3-2 win at San Siro and move up into fourth in Serie A with manager Ruben Amorim remaining unbeaten in his first seven league games.
articles.headlineJa: ルーベン・アモリム、ミラン勝利によりセリエAで無敗を維持
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランはサン・シーロでアタランタの反撃を凌ぎ切り3-2で勝利。セリエAで4位に浮上し、監督のルーベン・アモリムはリーグ戦最初の7試合で無敗を継続している。
articles.body:
AC Milan held off a fightback from Atalanta to close out a 3-2 win at San Siro and move up into fourth in Serie A with manager Ruben Amorim remaining unbeaten in his first seven league games.

The Rossoneri, who had won 4-0 away at RB Salzburg in the Europa League on Thursday night, took the lead through Goncalo Ramos' penalty, with Adrien Rabiot slotting in a second just before the break.

Ramos then saw another spot kick saved, but Mario Gila made it 3-0 on the hour, before Atalanta fought back with goals from Gianluca Gaetano and Nikola Krstovic, however, they could not find an equaliser.

Christian Pulisic saw his early goal from close range ruled out for a tight offside call following a VAR check.

Milan then did get themselves in front after 24 minutes.

Atalanta substitute Relja Obric, who had not long been sent on for his league debut to replace injured defender Sead Kolasinac, turned to block Yunus Musah's shot, but the ball struck his outstretched hand.

After reviewing the incident on the pitchside monitor, the referee awarded a penalty, which Ramos coolly dispatched by sending Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi the wrong way.

Milan doubled their lead just before halftime when Diego Moreira found Rabiot at the edge of the area and he cut inside before drilling a low shot back into the bottom corner.

The home side was awarded another penalty in the 56th minute following a VAR review after a handball by Thomas Kristensen from Rabiot's volley. Carnesecchi, though, this time guessed right to parry Ramos' spot kick.

From the resulting corner, Gila headed in at the back post off Rabiot's flick-on to seemingly put the result beyond doubt.

Atalanta, though, rallied after substitute Gaetano showed neat control in the six-yard box to pull a goal back in the 66th minute and then Krstovic further reduced the deficit after a swift counter attack with nine minutes left, but Ruben Amorim's side dug in to see out the closing stages.

Milan, led by former Manchester United coach Amorim, are one of four teams undefeated in Serie A, along with rival Inter Milan, Lazio and Roma.

Information from PA and The Associated Press was used in this recap.

articles.headline: Knicks waive Bruce Brown, keep James Wiseman ahead of opener
articles.description: The Knicks are waiving Bruce Brown and keeping James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: ニックス、ブルース・ブラウンを放出、ジェームズ・ウィズマンは開幕に向けて残留
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNが報じたところによると、ニックスはレギュラーシーズン開幕を控え、ブルース・ブラウンを放出する一方で、ジェームズ・ウィズマンをロスターに留めることを決定した。
articles.body:
The New York Knicks waived Bruce Brown and will keep James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener.

Brown was one of several players on non-guaranteed deals vying for one of New York's final two available roster spots. Tony Bradley, Ochai Agbaji and Drew Eubanks were all also waived in recent days.

Wiseman appeared in all four of the Knicks' preseason games and impressed in 24 minutes vs. the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday, when he scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds.

 

According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, the Knicks could have kept Brown and Wiseman, but because they are only $3.2 million below their self-imposed hard cap at the second apron, retaining both players would've been difficult.  

Wiseman, 25, will join Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond in New York's center rotation. The reigning NBA champions lost key reserve big man Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics this past summer via free agency.

The Knicks begin the NBA's regular season Tuesday, when they host the new-look Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.headline: 76ers, needing frontcourt help, convert 7-foot-6 Tacko Fall to two-way contract
articles.description: The 76ers, dealing with injuries in the frontcourt, have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract.
articles.headlineJa: フロントコートの補強を必要とする76ers、7フィート6インチのタコ・フォールとツーウェイ契約を締結
articles.descriptionJa: フロントコートでの怪我に悩まされている76ersは、センターのタコ・フォールをツーウェイ契約に切り替えた。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The 76ers have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract, the team announced Saturday.

Last month, the Sixers signed the 7-foot-6 center to an Exhibit 10 deal, and injuries to the frontcourt likely led to Fall getting this spot.

Ariel Hukporti, projected to be the Sixers' backup center, suffered a season-ending right Achilles tear in the preseason. Center Adem Bona, potentially the next man up, has been sidelined with a foot injury, and Dominick Barlow has battled back soreness that kept him out of the preseason.

Fall hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season, when he was with the Cleveland Cavaliers. This will be his fourth season in the NBA. He played his first two in Boston with new Sixers forward Jaylen Brown.

Fall, 30, most recently played for the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association.

articles.headline: James, Embiid play 76ers' preseason finale, 'still working on our rhythm'
articles.description: Without VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday night's 125-120 loss to the Celtics, 76ers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what his team may look like this season, including LeBron James and Joel Embiid playing preseason highs in minutes.
articles.headlineJa: ジェームズとエンビード、76ersのプレシーズン最終戦に出場、「まだリズムを掴もうとしているところ」
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜夜のセルティックス戦（120-125で敗戦）を欠場したVJ・エッジコムが不在の中、76ersのニック・ナース監督は、レブロン・ジェームズとジョエル・エンビードがプレシーズン最多の出場時間を記録するなど、今シーズンのチーム像を最も具体的に示す形となった。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- As the 76ers begin a season with a star-laden roster, center Joel Embiid rejects the narrative that anyone needs to sacrifice for this team to succeed.

"I'm against the concept of sacrificing," Embiid said after Friday's preseason finale. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat."

Albeit without second-year starting guard VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday's 125-120 loss to the Boston Celtics for precautionary reasons, Sixers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what his team may look like this season.

The other active Sixers starters -- LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Embiid -- all played preseason highs in minutes and well into the second half. Embiid, who struggled in his last appearance two games ago against the Brooklyn Nets, finishing with six points and eight turnovers, was dominant.​

He scored 27 points, grabbed eight rebounds and added five assists. In the third quarter, he had one of the game's highlights when he threw down an emphatic dunk that drew roars from fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"It's good to dunk. I thought I would never dunk again," Embiid said with a smile. "I guess I don't know what happened. I kind of got possessed."

Still, the group never looked comfortable together on the floor, despite playing against Celtics reserves. After the game, players didn't shy away from their somewhat disjointed performance. Brown pointed to the team's spacing Friday night, which he said led to turnovers, as one of the many things they need to fix moving forward.

"We're not where we want to be yet," he said. "So that's just a part of it. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day."

James echoed Brown's comments, but neither seemed concerned about the Sixers' ability to eventually jell.

"We're getting there," James said. "I mean, obviously we are a couple of weeks in, so we're still working on our rhythm, working on our kinks, and it's not going to be perfect."

The Sixers open the regular season against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.

articles.headline: No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa injures ankle during Wizards' preseason finale
articles.description: First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Wizards' preseason finale after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.
articles.headlineJa: ドラフト1位指名のAJ・ディバンツァ、ウィザーズのプレシーズン最終戦で足首を負傷
articles.descriptionJa: 全体1位指名のAJ・ディバンツァが、ウィザーズのプレシーズン最終戦で不自然な着地により足首を負傷して途中交代した。今後、詳細な検査を受ける予定。
articles.body:
First overall pick AJ Dybantsa exited the Washington Wizards' preseason finale Friday after injuring his ankle on an awkward landing and will undergo further evaluation.

Wizards coach Brian Keefe told sideline reporter Chase Hughes that Dybantsa had suffered a mild ankle sprain but that the decision to keep him out for the rest of the game was more precautionary.

"We'll look at it more when we get more information," Keefe said.

Dybantsa fell to the ground after landing on his left ankle following a midrange jump shot before limping to the locker room. He had scored 12 points in 15 minutes before his exit in the second quarter.

The Wizards open the regular season Wednesday against the Milwaukee Bucks.
